faqs.a: The last two digits of an 8-digit HEX are the alpha channel in base 16. 80 hex = 128 decimal, and 128/255 = 0.50, so the color is 50% opaque. FF is fully opaque, 00 is fully transparent.
Use rgba() when you need the widest compatibility and readable code. Use 8-digit HEX when you want compact values, for example in design tokens. They describe the same color.
faqs.q: Should I use rgba() or 8-digit HEX?

faqs.a: Yes — paste codes like #4f46e580. The tool detects the 8-digit form and reads the alpha from the last two digits; the opacity slider is then ignored because the code already defines transparency.
faqs.q: Can I paste an 8-digit HEX as input?

faqs.a: At 0% the color is fully transparent — invisible on the checkerboard, which is correct behavior. The rgba() and 8-digit HEX values are still valid and copyable.

keyFacts: RGBA adds an alpha channel (0 to 1) to any RGB color.
8-digit HEX stores alpha in its last two base-16 digits.
100% opacity means fully opaque; 0% means fully transparent.
The checkerboard background is the standard way to preview transparency.
Pasting an 8-digit HEX lets the code itself define the alpha.

hex-to-rgba-converter.workedExample:
Convert #4f46e5 at 50% opacity.
HEX pairs: 4f = 79, 46 = 70, e5 = 229.
Alpha = 50/100 = 0.50.
rgba() result: rgba(79, 70, 229, 0.5).
8-digit HEX: round(0.50 x 255) = round(127.5) = 128 = 0x80, so #4f46e580.
Both values describe the same semi-transparent indigo.
